key_facts: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said at Wednesday's press conference that the Fed will not commit to a set policy course: "If we had a firm conclusion about the conduct of monetary policy, we'd announce it to much fanfare today." He also said financial conditions are tighter but he is "unwilling and unable to call them tight." The FOMC held rates flat in June and July, then raised them in September, with inflation well above the 2% target.

Warsh announced the Fed will keep meeting eight times a year but skip rate votes at one meeting in 2027 and two in 2028. Regional presidents will also get one fewer scheduled vote in their year-long rotations. The chair retains authority to call an impromptu meeting.
Robert Sockin (PGIM, chief US economist) called holding rates this week a "policy mistake" and said a gradual Fed likely means one that has to hike higher, raising recession risk.
Analysis notes the next FOMC meeting is in December; Warsh said inflation target is 2% flat, not a range in the twos.

key_facts: The UK government changed HMRC rules so that certain lump sum pension death benefits from the Civil Service Pension scheme will no longer become taxable solely because they are paid more than two years after the scheme was notified of a death. The change was announced in the Budget and applies to payments made from 28 October.

Under previous rules, a lump sum death benefit paid to someone who died before age 75 was tax-free only if paid within two years of notification and below the Lump Sum and Death Benefit Allowance. Administrator Capita, which took over from MyCSP in December 2025, reported a backlog of over 86,000 cases, grown to 120,000 by February; 1,643 bereavement or death-in-service cases were over 100 days old as of 30 September, per the latest figures cited.

One beneficiary, Rob Wassell, received a delayed lump sum after two years and was taxed at 45%; he is awaiting a complaint review on reimbursement. Pensions minister Torsten Bell said affected people may seek compensation via the scheme's complaints process and the Pensions Ombudsman.
importance_reason: Narrow change to tax treatment of death benefits for a specific public-sector pension scheme with limited direct market effect.
